edges.effect_quant: Anti-androgen therapy improves PCOS-related hirsutism, and spironolactone is one of the main contributors to that signal. A PCOS-specific 2023 meta-analysis found anti-androgens plus lifestyle superior to metformin plus lifestyle for hirsutism (WMD -1.59, 95% CI -3.06 to -0.12). A broader Cochrane review also found spironolactone more effective than placebo for Ferriman-Gallwey score reduction (MD -7.69, 95% CI -10.12 to -5.26).
edges.population: women with polycystic ovary syndrome or clinically relevant hyperandrogenic hirsutism treated with spironolactone
edges.mechanism: Spironolactone reduces hirsutism mainly through androgen receptor antagonism and partial inhibition of androgen production, which decreases terminal hair growth in androgen-sensitive areas over time.
edges.summary: This is a reasonable protective edge with good clinical face validity. The direct PCOS literature is not huge and often groups spironolactone with other anti-androgens, but the overall evidence still supports spironolactone as an effective option for reducing hirsutism severity when contraception and safety monitoring are in place.
edges.caveats: Much of the pooled evidence is anti-androgen class-based rather than spironolactone-only, and cosmetic improvement takes months rather than weeks. The evidence is therefore supportive but not perfectly isolated to one drug in one phenotype.

evidence.notes: Efficacy and safety of anti-androgens in the management of polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
